_comment: The opening crawl, one per side. Sean, 22 September: a Star Wars text scroll — one short sentence a slide, an image behind each, scrolled through before the first day. Written at about a fifth-grade reading level on purpose: a player arriving with no knowledge should finish it knowing what the world is, why the war started, and what they have to do to win.
_stance: Rewritten 22 September on Sean's correction: **each side makes its own case and only its own.** No 'they say this, we say that'. The Crown never mentions what the Confederacy wants; the Confederacy never repeats the Crown's argument about a golden age, it simply disavows them. The only thing both scrolls contain is the Drowning, because neither side disputes that it happened.
_warning: THE OBJECTIVE SLIDES DO NOT MATCH `checkVictory` YET. Sean's 22 September brief gives the Crown 'round up their leaders and take their hidden port' and the Confederacy 'take Highwater and the boy emperor with it'. The code today wins the Crown's war on all three Pirate Lords captured at once, and the Confederacy's on the Lord Regent and Admiral Blackwater captured at once — Freeport and Highwater are not win conditions, and there is no emperor character. This is his call to make and is flagged in docs/opening-scroll.md. Do not ship the scroll to players until the copy and the rules agree.
_art: `art` is a slug under src/art/scroll/. Where no painting exists the screen falls back to the drawn scene for that faction, the way portraits and ships already do. `brief` is the note for whoever paints it and is never shown to a player.

slides.text: Long ago all of this was one land, and the legends say it was glorious.
slides.brief: A wide green country under a low sun, roads and cities on it. No sea anywhere in frame. Painted like a memory somebody is describing rather than a place anybody has been.

slides.text: Then the ice let go, and the sea rose for a thousand years.
slides.brief: Ice calving into dark water, the horizon already higher than it should be. Cold light.

slides.text: Our people climbed to the high ground of the Sovereign Reach.
slides.brief: A long column of people and carts on a mountain road at dusk, water behind and below them.

slides.text: The greatest peak became the Aldermain, and its greatest city is Highwater.
slides.brief: Highwater in Imperial green and gold: seawalls, a lit channel, a fleet at anchor in good order. Civilized and impressive, never sinister.

slides.text: After centuries of warlords, one man united the island and founded the Crown Imperium.
slides.brief: The Emperor's standard raised over a field of broken warlord banners. Ceremony, not slaughter.

slides.text: He died this year, and left his son a throne and a dying wish — every Reach under one flag.
slides.brief: A boy in oversized state robes on a too-large chair, the Admiralty standing behind him. Sympathetic, not comic.

slides.text: Pirates burned our greatest shipyard and named themselves enemies of the Crown.
slides.brief: Yarrow Minor burning at night, seen from a Crown deck. Five slipways under one roof, and the roof going.

slides.text: Round up their leaders. Find their hidden port and take it.
slides.brief: Three faces on a warrant sheet under a lamp, and a chart with one stretch of water left blank.

slides.text: Through trade, duty, and discipline — a safer world.
slides.brief: The Crown sigil over a calm working harbour at dawn: a crown above a fouled anchor, compass star behind.

slides.text: The legends say the world was one land, before the ice melted and the sea rose for a thousand years.
slides.brief: The same painting the Crown's scroll opens on. Deliberately identical: neither side disputes this part.

slides.text: What the water left us was a thousand islands.
slides.brief: Warm water, scattered green rocks to the horizon, small craft between them. Bright where the Crown's version of the same moment is cold.

slides.text: On every one of them a people grew up with their own way of living.
slides.brief: Four boats in one frame that share nothing: a coral-grown hull, an Urskin whaler, a bog punt, a Shoal outrigger.

slides.text: The Crown Imperium means to end that, and make every island the same.
slides.brief: A licensing writ nailed to a boat shed, a marine's back turned, a dredger in the water behind and the coral gone white.

slides.text: Three captains would not have it, and the Free Confederacy was born.
slides.brief: The articles on a table at Freeport, a dozen hands signing, lamplight. Three figures standing over it.

slides.text: Our first blow burned their greatest shipyard to the waterline.
slides.brief: The same fire as the Crown's slide seven, from the water this time and further off — small boats pulling away from a burning yard.

slides.text: They answered by swearing to take every Reach by force.
slides.brief: A Crown line of battle coming over the horizon in good order, seen from a low deck. Numerous and unhurried.

slides.text: Break their fleet. Take Highwater, and their boy emperor with it.
slides.brief: Highwater's wall from below at night, one lit window near the top, small figures at the foot of it.
The Confederate mark on a patched red sail against open water: skull in a red headscarf, crossed cutlasses, compass star.
